Title: MCMC probes Threads content insulting Negri Sembilan royal institution
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negri Sembilan.
MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
As part of the investigation, MCMC recorded a statement from a person at the Labu police station.
"Also seized was a mobile phone along with an eSIM for forensic analysis. The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998," it said in a statement.
MCMC is also examining how the content was disseminated across social media platforms and will work with relevant enforcement agencies should other offences under existing laws warrant action.
MCMC said that freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly, in accordance with the law and with respect for the royal institution.
The commission added that any enforcement action will be carried out based on facts, evidence and due legal process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 Indonesians jailed for using fake passport stamps
Article:
PASIR MAS: Four Indonesians were sentenced to five months' jail each by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to using fake stamps on their passports when entering Malaysia.
The four, identified as Rahmawati, 39, Rahma, 52, Sumkiah, 57, and Ahmad Rifat Ramadani, 20, were found to have used the fake stamps while travelling on an express bus on Oct 10.
All four pleaded guilty before judge Zulkpli Abdullah.
They were charged under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
The judge ordered the jail terms to take effect from the date of their arrest.
In the same court, 29 other undocumented migrants were charged with various immigration offences.
They comprised 24 Indonesians, two Bangladeshis, two Myanmar nationals and one Vietnamese. All pleaded guilty to their charges.
Of the 29, 22 were sentenced to three months' jail and fined RM10,000 each.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 11pct of screened Kelantan toddlers found stunted
Article:
KOTA BARU: A total of 769 out of 2,688 3-year-olds screened in Kelantan were found to have health issues, including being underweight and stunted.
Kelantan Health Department director Dr Kasuadi Hussin said screenings conducted across 10 districts found that 9.8 per cent of the children were underweight, 10.9 per cent were stunted, 0.3 per cent were not fully immunised and 9.6 per cent had not received exclusive breastfeeding.
"The screening programme aims to identify and map the actual extent of incomplete immunisation and stunting among 3-year-olds in Kelantan, enabling targeted clinical and community interventions," he told reporters after launching the 2026 state-level Wellness Month carnival and Children's Health Day celebration here today.
Dr Kasuadi said being underweight could result from several factors, including insufficient food intake, calorie deficiency and unhealthy dietary habits, such as excessive consumption of junk food.
He said stunting could be influenced by genetics, nutrition and a family's socioeconomic background, particularly among the Orang Asli community.
"That is why we must identify the root causes so that appropriate interventions can be provided," he said, adding that stunting could be managed through growth monitoring and a balanced diet.
He urged parents to take their children for regular health check-ups at nearby clinics to ensure health issues were detected and treated early.
He said check-ups should continue until children were six or seven years old, before they entered primary school.
"Children's health problems can be detected early through screenings. The earlier we detect them, the sooner action can be taken," he said.

Title: Zelenskyy says Russia attacked Ukrainian energy sector 76 times in past week
Article:
KYIV: Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors dozens of times in the week since US President Donald Trump announced a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday.
"Since the American President announced the energy ceasefire a week ago, Russia has deliberately attacked Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors 76 times," he wrote on X, adding the latest strikes hit substations in the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, and Odesa regions.
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy described Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on its goods days before they were to take effect will embolden Moscow to keep attacking Ukraine.
Zelenskyy also predicted even more US sanctions relief.
"The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskyy wrote on X. "It definitely helps only the Russians."
An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs — including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas — that had been scheduled to start next week under the legislation known as the Graham Act that he signed into law last month.
Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the United States.
The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022.
Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticising Zelenskyy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader.
Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskyy.
"This certainly does not stop the war."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib house arrest rules in final drafting stage
Article:
BESUT: The Prisons Department is in the final stages of drafting rules and conditions for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the department, which is responsible for implementing Pardons Board decisions, had received a letter from the board's secretariat setting out the decision and related conditions.
"Specific rules on house arrest need to be drafted because this mechanism has never been implemented before.
"The drafting process is now in its final stages," he told reporters at the launch of the National Anti-Drug Agency's Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes in Felda Tenang.
Saifuddin said the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat also stated that the Prisons Department could set any appropriate conditions.
He said Najib had yet to pay the RM50 million fine and was still serving his sentence in prison.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry, particularly the Prisons Department, was responsible for preparing rules to ensure that house arrest was governed by clear conditions.
"That is all I can comment on for now," he said.
On Sept 18, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
The
decision was made
at the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm warning in 10 states, 2 FTs until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 10 states and two Federal Territories until 6pm today.
MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Baling, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Padang Terap and Sik, while in Penang, they are Seberang Prai Selatan, Seberang Prai Tengah and Seberang Prai Utara.
In Perak, the warning covers Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Larut, Matang and Selama, and Kerian.
In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.
In Negri Sembilan, the warning covers Seremban and Jelebu.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman (Lingga and Pantu), Betong (Kabong and Pusa), and Kuching. In Sabah, they are Kudat (Kota Marudu and Kudat), the West Coast and the Interior.

Title: E-commerce Bill to be tabled in March
Article:
KUANTAN: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, will be tabled at the first parliamentary sitting next year.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the draft was ready and being revised.
"Currently, we do not have specific legislation governing e-commerce. In most cases, we facilitate negotiations by acting as intermediaries between
online entrepreneurs or sellers and marketplaces,
" she told reporters after the closing ceremony of the retail access programme here today.
Fuziah also said 1,862 entrepreneurs had received assistance under the retail access programme from 2023 to October this year.
The programme helps micro-entrepreneurs showcase their products, understand supermarket requirements and identify opportunities to enter the retail market.
Parliament will convene for its first sitting in March next year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget, announced that the government would
introduce the Bill
to regulate e-commerce platforms operating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Never seen anything like it': Mass looting grips Paris
Article:
SMASHING shop windows and snatching boxes of goods, looters in Paris poured into stores across the capital on Saturday, facing no resistance from authorities as nationwide protests degenerated into violence.
Crowds of masked men wearing black hoodies yanked at metal store shutters until they gave way, clearing shelves of cigarettes, sunglasses, clothes, jewellery and food.
The violence erupted as hundreds of thousands of demonstrators gathered across the country to denounce the cost of living, following weeks of student protests and stoking political uncertainty six months before France's presidential election.
AFP journalists saw looters emerging from a supermarket carrying bags stuffed with cakes, fruit juice and alcohol.
From a small jewellery shop across the street, they took antique clocks. On a street corner, entire display racks of sunglasses vanished.
Inside the shops, they searched for the cash register, smashing it onto the floor, sometimes only to discover it was empty.
Perched on a pavement terrace with a colleague, a 38-year-old art teacher who gave her name as Alma said she had "never seen anything like it."
The pair, who had joined an unsuccessful march earlier in the day to reach the French president's residence, the Elysee Palace, said nonetheless that they "understand" the revolt.
The violence began on the sidelines of marches in the capital and other cities that the interior ministry said were attended by 550,000 people.
The CGT union, which took part, said 800,000 people participated.
[[nid:1558270]]
Police used tear gas and water cannon against protesters who threw projectiles and aimed fireworks.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who slammed the "violence of extreme intensity", said late Saturday that 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers hurt.
Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said whole streets "have been devastated" in the capital, making a distinction between the "fundamental" right to protest and "unacceptable" violence.
"I understand why people might be upset, but I think damaging property is fine, as long as we don't physically harm anyone," Alma said.
Restaurants, hotels and residential buildings have mostly been spared, prompting surreal scenes of Parisians enjoying their usual Saturday lunch with friends while crowds wreaked havoc outside.
Locals watched the scenes unfold from the safety of their apartments.
"What a sight," said Jules, a 29-year-old civil servant.
"They must have some pretty deep anger. They're a part of society who doesn't feel integrated."
While he agreed with the right to protest, he said the looters were "undermining their own goals."
"Just look at the state of the street," he told AFP.
Near the iconic Place de la Republique in central Paris, broken glass and debris littered the roads, as a pile of burning bicycles belched out thick smoke.
Law enforcement was absent from the area, having clashed with protesters there earlier in the day.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka election: Nine seats may see new faces
Article:
AYER KEROH: At least nine sitting state assemblymen in Melaka could be dropped ahead of the upcoming state election, paving the way for fresh faces.
The potential candidate reshuffle is driven by performance, tenure, seat allocation strategies, and party plans to expand influence, making the positions of at least nine incumbents a focus ahead of official candidate announcements starting next week.
Seats expected to see changes include Kuala Linggi, Rembia, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pengkalan Batu, Kesidang, Bemban, Serkam, and Sungai Rambai.
In Kuala Linggi, Datuk Rosli Abdullah's position is under scrutiny as Barisan Nasional weighs his experience and grassroots support against the need for candidate renewal.
In Rembia, Datuk Muhamad Jailani Khamis of Pas may see his position tested if the party fields a new candidate to boost its winning prospects in a shifting political landscape.
For Gadek, MIC incumbent Datuk VP Shanmugam faces uncertainty over whether the party will retain him or field a new candidate to draw multiracial support under BN.
In Sungai Udang, Melaka Umno deputy chairman and Paya Rumput incumbent Datuk Rais Yasin has been strongly linked to the seat.
This leaves current Sungai Udang assemblyman Dr Mohd Aleef Yusof of Parti Wawasan Negara in a delicate position, especially if political understandings between BN and Perikatan Nasional require him to make way for a BN candidate.
In Pengkalan Batu, incumbent Datuk Kalsom Nordin faces uncertainty. While her five-year service has been commendable, age factors may prevent the Melaka Umno Wanita chief from defending her seat.
DAP is also expected to make changes in Kesidang, where incumbent Allex Seah Shoo Chin may be dropped to make way for state DAP chairman and Kota Melaka member of parliament Khoo Poay Tiong to contest under the Pakatan Harapan banner.
This follows Kota Melaka Umno's stated readiness to field a BN candidate to wrest the seat from DAP.
In Bemban, incumbent Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub of Wawasan faces questions over his candidacy amid political realignments within the opposition, while in Serkam, three-term incumbent Datuk Zaidi Attan may be replaced as the party considers balancing experience with new blood.
In Sungai Rambai, incumbent Datuk Siti Faizah Abdul Azis noted her position is not guaranteed until official announcements are made, adding that she remains focused on serving her constituents.
Overall, candidate selection will test parties' ability to balance loyalty to incumbents, grassroots expectations and the need to field candidates with strong electoral prospects.
In a multi-cornered contest, decisions to retain or drop incumbents could affect not only individual candidates but also their parties' overall strength in the state.
However, the names remain speculative until the respective party leaderships make official announcements.
With nomination day approaching, attention is now on how far the parties' final calculations will reshape the line-up of incumbents defending their seats.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 for polling in the Melaka state election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
BN is scheduled to announce its candidate lineup on Oct 28, while PH and PN are expected to do so four days earlier.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: QR payment charges from Nov 1 claim is fake, says MOF
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Finance Ministry (MOF) today dismissed as false claims that service charges for quick response (QR) code payments would be introduced on Nov 1, as stated in a viral poster.
In a Facebook post, the ministry said that no official announcement had been made about imposing QR code payment service charges, as the poster claimed.
"The public is advised not to believe or share the poster claiming that QR payment service charges will be introduced on Nov 1, 2026, as the information is false," the statement said.
The MOF advised the public to verify information through its official channels before sharing it to prevent the spread of fake news that could mislead the public.
The poster had circulated widely on Facebook and Threads earlier, drawing mixed reactions and comments from social media users.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two Saudi pilots killed in helicopter crash near Yemen border
Article:
RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis on Sunday said two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the Iran-backed group said it shot the aircraft down.
The coalition blamed a "technical malfunction" for the incident, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running war with the Houthis reignited in July.
The incident comes a week after strikes by the Iran-backed group killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
"An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the Ministry of National Guard crashed inside Saudi territory in Najran Region due to a technical malfunction," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency.
"The accident resulted in the martyrdom of its aircrew, consisting of two officers."
Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.
After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen's conflict has surged back to life and intensified when the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis have hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International airport.
The Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi territory.
The coalition said overnight that it intercepted two drones in the Riyadh area and a third over the oil-rich Eastern Province. Saudi authorities had earlier issued a threat alert in the capital.
Two ballistic missiles "launched by the Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait" were intercepted in the kingdom's south, the coalition added.
On Saturday, the Houthis reported that Saudi strikes killed 12 people in Yemen, including three children.
The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and captured territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf's Strait of Hormuz.
On Sunday, Egypt's parliament will hold an emergency session after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi asked lawmakers to authorise support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
Sisi said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.
"I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," he said on Saturday. "We are speaking only about defence."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pangkor hit by flash floods in nine areas
Article:
IPOH: Flash floods triggered by more than two hours of continuous heavy rain early today affected nine areas on Pangkor Island.
The Perak Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the affected areas included Kampung Sungai Pinang Besar, Kampung Masjid, Kampung Teluk Kecil, Kampung Hussin, Teluk Gedung and Kampung Tengah.
Other affected locations were the Rumah Murah area, Taman Pangkor Mutiara and Taman Sri Pangkor.
The secretariat said the floods were first reported at 5.30am and were caused by continuous heavy rain rather than high tide.
"Floodwaters had completely receded by 2pm today, and residents are now cleaning their homes," it said.
Meanwhile, the flood situation in Larut, Matang and Selama has also improved, with three temporary relief centres (PPS) closing at 1.30pm today.
The centres were at SK Changkat Ibol, Dewan Masjid Al-Wusta Batu 8 and Dewan Perdana Trong.
However, two other PPS at SK Matang and SK Matang Gelugor remain operational.
The two centres are sheltering 146 flood victims from 48 families.

Title: Graduate salary floor must balance pay and jobs, economists say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed mandatory minimum starting salary for graduates should reflect job responsibilities, skills and productivity, while balancing higher wages against employers' ability to sustain recruitment, economists said.
The Human Resources Ministry will introduce guidelines on starting salaries for graduates and semi-skilled workers by June 2027, following the government's announcement of a proposed RM2,500 minimum starting salary under Budget 2027.
Its minister, Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, said the guidelines would provide employers and workers with a reference for
basic starting salaries
based on occupations, educational qualifications and skills.
Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Business and Management senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said clear eligibility criteria were essential to improve graduate wages without reducing employment opportunities.
He said the government should consider employers' financial capacity, particularly among small and medium enterprises (SMEs), before making the proposed salary requirements compulsory.
"Some employers, particularly SMEs, may become more cautious about hiring fresh graduates if the mandatory salary exceeds what they can justify based on current productivity," he told the New Straits Times.
Businesses might respond by reducing recruitment, prioritising experienced candidates or automating certain tasks, he said.
Idham called for phased implementation or targeted assistance for businesses struggling to meet the proposed requirements. He said wage reforms should also be supported by productivity improvements, professional training and stronger collaboration between industries and educational institutions.
While a salary floor could improve graduates' purchasing power amid rising living costs, he cautioned that higher wages alone would not resolve graduate underemployment.
"The ultimate measure of success is not simply whether graduates receive higher wages, but whether they gain better employment opportunities without being priced out of the labour market," he said.
Putra Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Ida Md Yasin said a minimum starting salary of RM2,500 would provide welcome financial relief for fresh graduates and could serve as a benchmark.
However, employers seeking workers with specialised knowledge and skills might need to offer higher salaries.
"Employers are also competing to attract good workers. If a job requires specialised skills or knowledge, RM2,500 may be too low, and companies may be willing to pay more," she said.
Ida said that higher labour costs could affect some SMEs and potentially lead to higher prices for goods and services.
She cautioned against assuming all SMEs would struggle to meet the proposed salary floor, as their financial capacity varied according to business performance and profit margins.
"Some SMEs have good profit margins and can afford to pay RM2,500 or even more to fresh graduates. It depends on the nature of their business and the type of work involved," she said.
Ida said the government should consider differences across industries and job requirements before making the guidelines mandatory.
She said salaries should reflect the knowledge and skills required for each position, particularly as routine and repetitive tasks could increasingly be performed through mechanisation or automation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians recount tense moments caught in Paris riots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian caught in Paris riots yesterday recounted tense moments when a mob of rioters left him trapped in traffic.
Ozil Zainal, in a post on Threads, said he was driving into Paris after finding that traffic heading into the city was relatively light.
"While driving along a road, all vehicles suddenly stopped as rioters passed through the area.
"The other drivers and I could not move. We were trapped with no way out on either side.
"We had to wait until the situation gradually calmed down and traffic began to flow again. Security personnel, including firefighters and ambulances, were seen rushing to the scene of the riots," said Ozil, adding that the riots had destroyed a lot of public property.
Another Malaysian who happened to be in Paris also shared her tense experience while shopping at a luxury brand boutique.
In a post on Threads, Lili Abroad said she was thankful that she had managed to leave the riot-hit area quickly before the situation worsened.
"When I was in LV (Louis Vuitton boutique), the doors of the premises were locked and several other boutiques also closed their doors," she said.
She said she had received more information about the demonstration from her sources and had started shopping earlier.
"The riots were estimated to have started at 5pm," said Lili, who has since left for southern France for other matters.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khairul Razikin, who is based in Limoges, France, said in a Threads post that he was saddened to learn that an iconic building in the city had also been targeted in yesterday's riots.
He said the Hôtel de Ville de Limoges, about five minutes from his home, had been destroyed by fire.
"This building has stood magnificently since 1883. It is sad to see what has happened today," he said.
A wave of riots and mass
protests
has swept several European countries since September, with demonstrations escalating in major cities, including Paris and Milan, Italy, last Saturday (local time).
The unrest is believed to have been triggered by a combination of grievances, particularly over student welfare, declining public services and the rising cost of living.
The riots sparked some of the worst violence in France in decades.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia considers helicopters, water-bombing aircraft to fight Indonesia fires
Article:
AYER KEROH: Malaysia is considering deploying helicopters and water bombers to assist Indonesia in combating raging forest fires across the republic.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the proposed aid is being discussed by senior officials from both nations before being presented to the cabinet for approval.
He said the assistance under consideration includes deploying helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to support firefighting operations in affected areas.
"The Foreign Ministry secretary-general, National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general, and National Security Council director-general are holding talks with their respective counterparts on the matter," he said after closing the 10th National Conference of Persatuan Solidariti Nasional (PerSoNa) here today.
"The outcome of these discussions will be brought to the cabinet soon to seek approval for sending appropriate assistance."
On Friday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had said Malaysia stands ready to assist Indonesia following President Prabowo Subianto's decision to accept assistance offers from neighbouring countries.
Elaborating further, Mohamad said Malaysia cannot remain silent as the forest fires affect the region, but stressed that any aid operation must prioritise safety.
He said firefighting operations face severe challenges due to remote inland locations and thick haze severely impairing visibility.
"It is difficult to send trucks or other equipment because the fires are deep in the interior," he said.
"The remaining option is aerial firefighting, but aircraft also face difficulties flying due to dense haze.
"Visibility is reported to be below 50 metres, while the pollution index in Kalimantan has reached 1,000."
He added that these hazardous conditions previously forced a Japanese team involved in assistance efforts to return home after being unable to continue its mission.
Mohamad assured that Malaysia will ensure any aerial assistance is executed cautiously without endangering pilots and crew.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One night away, family returns to flood-hit home in Bukit Mertajam
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A security guard's quick trip to his hometown turned into panic after learning that his house in Kampung Kubang Semang here was inundated by flash floods yesterday.
Ab Ghani Abdullah, 49, said he and his family had returned to Perlis on Friday to spend the night.
He said before leaving, he moved several vehicles to higher ground as a precaution due to continuous rain, leaving only his motorcycle behind.
"We went back to the village for only one night, and we really had a bad feeling because it was raining everywhere.
"While I was sleeping at the village, I received a call from a friend who told me the water had risen around the house," he said when met at the temporary relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Seri Penanti here today.
He said he and his family rushed back and arrived around 10pm last night, but had to register at the relief centre as the road to his house was still under about one metre of water.
He said since moving to the area six years ago, his family has been hit by floods four times, resulting in damage to property and furniture as well as threats from venomous animals and short circuits.
"Yesterday, a large python was seen around the house.
"There is also the risk of other venomous animals and short circuits.
"That is why it is very dangerous to enter the house while the water is still high," he said, and he is now sheltering at the relief centre with four family members, including his younger sibling, who is a person with disabilities.
Meanwhile, factory manager Khairun Najwa Md Noor, 37, said she decided to bring her 78-year-old mother, who has cancer, to the relief centre for her safety and easier access to treatment.
"I live in a family home that is more than 100 years old with my mother, husband and two children.
"When it happened, the water rose very quickly. Even though the house has been renovated to cope with floods, we still could not do anything, and on top of that, there was a high tide.
"My mother is frail and has lost her sight. I was worried and asked her to move to the relief centre temporarily because there is a medical team here," she said.
Seberang Perai Tengah district officer and district disaster management committee chairman Datuk Kamarul Haizal Koderat said 36 victims from 10 families had been evacuated to the relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Seri Penanti.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Check API readings to assess air quality amid haze, says DoE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public has been advised to refer to official Air Pollutant Index (API) readings to determine actual air quality rather than relying on surrounding conditions alone.
Department of Environment (DoE) deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said API readings were based on measurements of air pollutants taken using specialised equipment.
She said the readings served as an important guide for the public to take appropriate steps to protect their health.
She said thick-looking haze did not necessarily indicate high levels of air pollution, as visibility was also affected by weather, humidity and the refraction of light by particles in the atmosphere.
"Sometimes we see the haze looking very thick, but the API reading is still at a moderate level.
"This happens because what we see with the naked eye does not necessarily reflect the actual level of air pollution.
"What we see is actually also influenced by weather, humidity and how the particles refract light," she said when contacted by Berita Harian today.
Continuous fires in Indonesia, which had shrouded several parts of Southeast Asia in toxic haze, had triggered the highest-level alert by Asean's regional climate and fire monitoring centre.
https://www.nst.com.my/world/region/2026/10/1557413/haze-triggers-highest-alert-level-southern-asean-region
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre issued the highest-level alert amid a high risk of severe transboundary haze in the region.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah said the DoE had carried out 3,433 monitoring and enforcement actions nationwide as of Oct 18 as part of efforts to control air pollution and prevent open burning.
She said agencies coordinated their response under the National Haze Action Plan, with the National Disaster Management Agency activating the Disaster Management Committee if API readings exceeded 150 for more than 24 hours.
She said the department had also stepped up preparedness through the implementation of the National Haze Action Plan and the National Open Burning Action Plan.
She said the integrated measures included monitoring API readings, detecting fire hotspots, tracking transboundary haze and increasing patrols and enforcement in areas at risk of open burning.
"This information helps the DoE assess the current situation and identify areas that need attention, especially high-risk areas such as peatland, landfill sites, agricultural areas and plantations," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI-generated nude images of schoolgirls: Five police reports lodged
Article:
SEREMBAN: Five police reports have been lodged over the circulation of AI-generated nude images of female students at a secondary school here, with more than 300 students reportedly affected.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the reports were lodged by parents between Aug 20 and 23 over the distribution of images allegedly featuring the faces of female students.
In a press conference today, lawyer Ng Kian Nam said the incident came to light on Aug 12, when a Form Two student found a smartphone without a password in the school surau and discovered the explicit images.
He said the student sent the images to her 17-year-old sister's Instagram account before returning the phone to its original location.
"The images showed the faces of female students edited to appear nude using artificial intelligence (AI).
"The phone was later found by a disciplinary teacher and was believed to belong to a Form Five student at the school.
Ng said the five police reports were lodged on Aug 20, including one by the parents of the student who found the phone.
He added that the images were reportedly circulated among students and allegedly sold through Telegram.
Ng said a meeting involving parents and the school management board was held, following which they agreed to contact the state Education Department.
A further meeting involving parents, the Parent-Teacher Association, the school management board, school representatives and education department officers was held on Sept 15.
"At the meeting, the school acknowledged and confirmed that more than 300 students were affected by this," he said.
Ng said the school had suspended the male student believed to own the phone, in line with departmental procedures.
However, he said parents had not been informed about the status of the images involving their daughters or given a full account of what had happened.
He also said the parents of the student who found the phone were dissatisfied after their two children were asked to sign an undertaking not to disclose the incident, failing which they could face disciplinary action.
Ng said a letter had been sent to the Jalan Campbell police station calling for a more comprehensive investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's diversified economy, fiscal buffers to cushion external shocks: Amir Hamzah
Article:
BANGKOK: Malaysia's diversified economy, resilient export markets and stronger fiscal buffers will help cushion external shocks and support its growth outlook for 2027, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Amir Hamzah said geopolitical tensions, shifting global trade patterns and economic uncertainty would remain key risks, but Malaysia is better positioned to withstand disruptions after adapting to previous crises, including the Russia-Ukraine war and ongoing trade tensions.
"Malaysia's total trade in the first eight months of this year rose 27 per cent compared with the same period last year, reflecting the resilience of our trade sector," he told Bernama in an interview here.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's economic base has broadened beyond commodities and oil and gas to include electrical and electronics, semiconductors, data centres and advanced manufacturing, reducing its reliance on any single sector.
"Our export markets are also diversified, with no single market accounting for more than 17 per cent of exports, allowing businesses to redirect trade towards better-performing markets. Malaysia has shown that it is very adaptable," he said.
Amir Hamzah is leading the Malaysian delegation to the International Monetary Fund-World Bank Group Annual Meetings, held here at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre in Bangkok.
He said shifting geopolitical alignments and the fragmentation of globalisation have made supply chain reliability increasingly important, presenting Malaysia with an opportunity to strengthen its position as a trusted manufacturing and trading hub.
"The government is strengthening domestic industrial ecosystems to enable manufacturers to source more components locally, reducing their exposure to disruptions in international supply chains.
"Malaysia maintains trade relations with major economies while adhering to international law and ensuring that foreign investments generate genuine value for the domestic economy," he said.
On fiscal preparedness, Amir Hamzah said reforms to strengthen public finances have given the government greater capacity to respond to external shocks.
He emphasised that the government's response to recent tensions in West Asia prioritised supply security while providing targeted assistance to affected groups, including through expanded financing support rather than relying solely on subsidies.
"The government is also mobilising private capital alongside public funds to support economic growth, including by encouraging government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to invest in strategic domestic industries without compromising commercial returns," he said.
Amir Hamzah shared that Malaysia's total approved investments reached RM431.8 billion last year, with foreign and domestic direct investments each accounting for about half, reflecting confidence among international and local investors.
He said stronger domestic investment, supported by diversified industries and export markets, would further reinforce Malaysia's economic resilience and help sustain growth amid an uncertain global outlook.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Long Lellang heli crash: Doctor's husband wants final report expedited
Article:
MIRI: The husband of a medical officer killed in the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, has urged authorities to expedite the release of the final investigation report.
Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, whose wife Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin was among five killed in the Sept 8 crash, said findings released so far remain preliminary.
"I was informed the final report would take longer to complete.
"However, I hope it can be released as soon as possible and that the findings will be transparent," he said when contacted today.
On Friday, a
preliminary report
released by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) revealed that the safety investigation is ongoing, with factual information gathered so far at an initial stage.
The report said investigators are continuing to examine flight operations, standard operating procedures, and the helicopter's maintenance history to gather evidence, assess safety measures, and identify underlying conditions.
The AAIB noted that its initial investigation identified no deficiencies involving the aircraft's airframe, maintenance, or pilot.
The crash claimed the lives of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; Dr Ainul, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JD Vance has yet to decide on 2028 US Presidential run
Article:
ISTANBUL: US Vice President JD Vance said he has not decided whether to run for president in 2028, acknowledging he could ultimately opt out despite being widely viewed as a leading contender to succeed President Donald Trump, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing CBS News.
Asked by CBS News' Tony Dokoupil during an hourlong town hall in Michigan, released Saturday night, whether he might not run, Vance replied, "Of course there's a chance."
He described himself as a procrastinator when facing major life decisions and said he would "have to think about it", citing his four young children and his wife, Usha Vance, who "has never loved politics" but "loves public service."
Trump has called Vance his "most likely" Republican successor.
Vance also defended the administration's economic and foreign policies, blaming former President Joe Biden's administration for neglecting manufacturing while acknowledging that reversing its decline would take time.
On the Iran conflict and elevated fuel costs, he said, "I recognise that gas prices are too high right now," adding, "When this conflict is over, we are going to see gas prices come down."
Defending Trump's Iran strategy, Vance argued that the US had "in some ways ... won decisively" but added that "the enemy gets a vote here." He said Washington was seeking a "final firm commitment from the Iranians that they're not going to rebuild their nuclear programme."
Vance also rejected allegations of presidential corruption, saying he had not seen "a single shred of evidence that (Trump) participates or sanctions in that corruption."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians in Italy, France advised to avoid protest sites
Article:
AYER KEROH: Malaysians travelling to Italy and France have been advised to avoid student protest sites amid concerns over their safety and the risk of arrest by the authorities.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said no travel restrictions had been imposed on either country so far.
However, he advised Malaysians to remain vigilant and stay away from areas where demonstrations were taking place.
He said the protests were generally confined to specific routes and locations rather than entire cities such as Paris and Rome.
"There are no travel restrictions at present, but we advise Malaysians to stay away from areas where student demonstrations are taking place daily.
"Travellers should also check the latest situation at their destinations and avoid areas identified as major protest routes," he said after closing the 10th National General Assembly of Persatuan Solidariti Nasional (Persona) today.
It was reported that tens of thousands of students in Italy had joined demonstrations demanding improvements to conditions in their schools.
The protests followed similar
demonstrations
in France, where students have been protesting against conditions in the country's education system since late September.
Although demonstrations across Italy were largely peaceful, protests in the northwestern city of Turin turned violent, with dozens of demonstrators throwing stones, glass bottles and flares at security personnel, according to witnesses.
Mohamad also advised Malaysians against participating in the demonstrations to avoid the risk of arrest.
He said Malaysians travelling abroad must respect local laws and refrain from activities that could jeopardise their safety.
"They are advised to keep abreast of developments and comply with instructions issued by the authorities throughout their stay in Italy and France," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Regional anxiety and historical echoes follow Japan's militarisation
Article:
LETTER:
Japan is on the road to full militarisation. Its military budget has exceeded nine trillion yen (US$68 billion), hitting the target of two per cent of GDP, though lagging behind the United States (US$1 trillion) and China (US$340 billion).
Japan has overhauled its post-World War II (WW2) defence export policies, lifting strict limits on export of lethal weapons.
In April 2026, it has permitted lethal weapons transfer to 17 eligible partners, including Indonesia and Philippines.
Talks are abuzz Tokyo may transfer several Oyashio-class submarines or advanced frigates to Indonesia.
Manila may receive several retired Abukuma class destroyer escorts from Japanese Maritime Defense Force.
Besides that, Tokyo has also gifted vessels for Philippine Coast Guard since Marcos Jnr took over the presidency and deployed approximately 1,400 combat-capable Self-Defence Force troops to participate alongside US and Philippine forces in major joint military exercises like the Balikpapan Exercise 2026, marking the first of its kind after WW2.
Tokyo has a joint programme with Italy and UK to co-develop a sixth-generation fighter jet. There are plans to co-manufacture the Mogami-class frigates with Australia after failing to sell the Soryu-class diesel submarines to replace the ageing Collins Class submarines in 2014.
In 2021 Australia cancelled the contract with a French Company and opted instead to accept the offer from US and UK. Under the AUKUS programme Australia will receive eight nuclear-powered submarines.
Japan's rush to rearm is mainly due to the anticipated US military draw down policy from the region.
Without the nuclear umbrella that gave protection to Japan's pacifist policy for over 80 years, Tokyo must upgrade its deterrence capabilities as insurance against an uncertain future.
Contrary to popular opinions, i do not believe Japan's renewed strategic ambitions was solely driven by China's rise.
It is driven more by the uncertainty about American protection and the decline of its primacy. In my view, Japan's militarisation programme is about achieving strategic autonomy that is no longer constrained by Article 9 of its Constitution.
A clause in Article 9 outlaws war as a means to settle international disputes involving the state.
Japan currently may feel the need of a strong military to deal with its potential strategic vulnerabilities in the region including a resurgent China, a major economic partner and an increasingly consequential military competitor.
Despite recent high level diplomatic overtures, Tokyo's relations with South Korea is complicated by the legacy of Japanese colonial rule.
Tokyo also view a nuclear-armed North Korea with missile capabilities as an adversary and concerned with the security of Taiwan it annexed in in 1895.
Taiwan's security is closely connected to Japan's geography, maritime approaches and alliance commitments.
What broke really the Japan's camel's back to rearm is the US, Japan's principal security ally whose protection could no longer be guaranteed.
However, the rise of Japan as a military power is likely to contribute to some anxiety in the region that has not forgotten the brutality of its Imperial Army.
While the region currently benefits from Japanese investment, trade and foreign aid last 30 years, the return of its military to the region is something else.
The region needs its money but not soldiers.
BA HAMZAH
Former lecturer
National Defence University Malaysia (UPNM)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal seeks legal changes to expedite death certificates for 54 missing Malaysians
Article:
MELAKA: Nepal is seeking to amend its laws to expedite the issuance of death certificates for 54 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following floods and landslides in the country in August.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Nepal's current laws require a waiting period of up to three years before death certificates can be issued for people who remain missing after a disaster.
He said representatives of the Nepali Embassy informed him of the matter during a visit to his office last week.
"The Nepali government is pursuing the legal amendments and will table them in Parliament. Failing that, it will make special arrangements to ensure death certificates can be issued without delay for the 54 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for," he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the National Solidarity Association's (PerSoNa) 10th National General Conference for the 2025 session here today.
Mohamad said the certificates were needed by the victims' families to settle related matters, including dealings with banks and insurance companies.
On Aug 26, flash floods and landslides struck Nepal's Rasuwa district and the Nepal-Tibet border area following heavy rain, damaging infrastructure and communications and hampering search-and-rescue operations.
The Foreign Ministry had earlier confirmed that a Malaysian who had been uncontactable after the disaster returned home safely on Oct 2, bringing the number of Malaysians still unaccounted for to 54.
Meanwhile, Mohamad said Malaysia was awaiting decisions by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the National Security Council (NSC) on assistance to tackle forest fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, Indonesia.
He said the outcome of the discussions would be brought to the cabinet for approval.
Efforts to extinguish the fires remained challenging because they were burning in remote areas amid thick haze, he added.
"Visibility is below 50 metres and the Air Pollutant Index in Kalimantan has reached 1,000," he said, adding that Malaysia would assess the risks before deciding whether to provide air support.
He said Malaysia would not deploy pilots if conditions posed a threat to their safety.
On the situations in Italy and France, Mohamad advised Malaysians travelling to the two countries to avoid demonstrations and areas where rioters had gathered.
He said there were currently no travel restrictions for either country, but Malaysians should remain cautious and follow local authorities' safety advice. -BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Storm, flash floods damage 23 houses in Pendang
Article:
PENDANG: A total of 23 houses in four villages here were affected by a storm, strong winds, and flash floods following heavy rain yesterday evening.
Pendang Civil Defence officer Yuslina Yusoff said the first report was received at 5.30pm before six Malaysian Civil Defence Force personnel were dispatched to the affected areas.
She said strong winds damaged the roofs of four houses in Kampung Bukit Pak Pom and three in Kampung Lahar Tunjang.
"The incident also caused several trees to fall, blocking the main road. However, no injuries or fatalities were reported," she said when contacted.
Meanwhile, Yuslina said flash floods affected 16 houses in two other villages, involving 13 homes in Kampung Baru, Mukim Padang Peliang, and three in Kampung Titi Akar, Mukim Padang Kerbau.
She said the flash floods were triggered by heavy rain in hilly areas at 5pm, sending fast-flowing water spilling into low-lying areas.
"The overflow also caused the main road to be inundated at 6.10pm. However, the water level trend shows a slow decline and the situation remains under control at this time," she said.
"Civil Defence Force personnel are at the location to monitor the situation, gather information, and advise at-risk residents to be ready to evacuate should conditions worsen."
She also reminded residents in high-risk areas to remain alert to weather changes and prioritise family safety throughout the rainy season.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze persists in KL despite rain as winds bring more pollution, says DoE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze continues to affect the capital despite recent rain, as winds carry smoke and pollutants into the country while high humidity and water vapour contribute to poor visibility.
The Batu Muda and Cheras monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 156 and 155 respectively at noon today.
Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DoE) director Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab said the rain was caused by natural weather conditions, not cloud seeding, and had only slightly reduced haze particles in areas where it fell.
"Winds are still carrying haze into the country, causing API readings to remain high in most areas," she told the New Straits Times.
She said Malaysia was currently in the monsoon transition phase, which typically brings thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds to the west coast and interior of the peninsula.
Although PM2.5 concentrations and API readings had decreased after the rain, poor visibility could make the haze appear more severe than the readings suggested, she added.
PM2.5 refers to fine particles measuring 2.5 micrometres or smaller that can penetrate deep into the lungs.
Sharifah Zakiah said high humidity and water vapour could trap dust and reduce visibility, particularly in the morning and after rain.
"This may lead people to assume that API readings should be higher than those recorded by DoE monitoring stations," she said.
She said PM2.5 remained the main pollutant at both Batu Muda and Cheras, with readings lower than before but still above pre-haze levels.
Despite the persistently unhealthy readings, the latest API trend showed a decline, she added.
The transboundary haze has
affected Malaysia's air quality
since Aug 8 and is expected to gradually ease over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said on Tuesday.
A
cloud-seeding operation
was conducted in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Selangor last month to mitigate the impact of the haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two killed, including 6-year-old, when truck drives through Kansas youth football match: Police
Article:
WASHINGTON:  A truck drove into a youth football match in Wichita, Kansas, leaving a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man dead, and 10 others hospitalised with traumatic injuries, police said on Saturday.
The injuries ranged from minor to severe, but none appear to be life-threatening, Wichita police Captain Aaron Moses said at a news conference. The two people killed were pronounced dead at the scene, he said.
Moses said a 34-year-old woman was driving the truck, which ended up in a field at the west end of the Stryker Sports Complex. She has been cooperating with investigators, he said, but when asked whether she had been arrested, he said only that she was in custody.
"We know what happened, but now we're working very hard to find out why it happened, and we're not there yet," Wichita police Chief Joe Sullivan said.
The injured include two youths aged 5, two aged 8, a 9-year-old and five adults, police said. In addition to those 10 people, one adult was hospitalised for non-traumatic medical issues.
The driver had a child playing football at the complex, but not on the field where the incident took place, Moses said. The truck involved had two juveniles as passengers, he said.
Emergency dispatchers started getting calls about the incident at 3.25pm local time (2025 GMT), Moses said.
"Today is a heartbreaking day for Wichita," Mayor Lily Wu said. "Families came to Stryker Sports Complex to enjoy a Saturday afternoon, watching their children play football  and no one could have imagined the tragedy that would unfold." — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vietnam signs free trade deal with four European nations
Article:
HANOI: Vietnam and four European nations outside the EU signed a free trade agreement in Hanoi on Sunday, seeking to diversify their markets as US tariffs disrupt global commerce.
The deal, between Southeast Asia's fastest-growing economy and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), which includes Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, eliminates or reduces customs duties, including on imports of industrial, fish and agricultural products.
The deal was signed in the capital in the presence of Vietnam's top leader To Lam and representatives of EFTA governments.
Vietnam said the agreement showed the parties' resolve to "reinforce the rules-based trading system amid continued volatility in the global economy", according to a government statement.
It was also expected to help Vietnam "diversify its import and export markets" and "integrate more deeply into global value chains", the government said.
Vietnam and EFTA concluded negotiations in July, more than a decade after the free trade talks officially began in 2012.
The parties relaunched negotiations in September last year, after they had stalled since 2018.
The agreement followed a global trade-disrupting tariff blitz by the United States under President Donald Trump which has left Vietnam with a hefty tax on its US exports amid ongoing negotiations with Washington.
Experts say the new deal reflected a shared initiative to diversify commercial ties and reduce reliance on major trading partners.
"As the US increasingly exerts trade pressure on European countries, the agreement is a joint effort to turn economic integration into greater strategic autonomy and to develop alternative commercial relationships rather than relying exclusively on their largest partners," history and politics scholar Do Dinh Lam Khang told AFP.
For Vietnam, closer ties with EFTA economies could support its ambition to move into higher-value-added activities, Khang added.
The agreement covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, trade remedies and sustainable development, among other areas, both parties say.
Bilateral trade between the EFTA and Vietnam last year was valued at 4.8 billion euros (US$5.4 billion), according to the association.
Electrical and mechanical machinery, fish and pharmaceutical products were the EFTA nations' top exports to Vietnam last year.
Machinery, footwear and apparel were manufacturing hub Vietnam's major exports to the EFTA.
The association was created as a counterpart to the European Economic Community, precursor of the European Union which its four member states are close to but have not joined.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan crisis will not affect BN's Melaka polls preparations – Tok Mat
Article:
MELAKA: The political situation in Negri Sembilan is not expected to affect Barisan Nasional's preparations for the Melaka election next month, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said the key is ensuring that strategies drawn up by party leadership are effectively executed by the election machinery to secure victory, noting that good strategies fail without proper implementation.
"We can draw up an excellent strategy that looks very good on paper, with many voters identified or categorised as BN's fixed supporters," he said.
"But if we fail to get them to turn out to vote, it means nothing. Their votes will not be cast."
Mohamad, who is also the foreign minister, said this after officiating at the closing of the 10th National Conference of Persatuan Solidariti Nasional (PerSoNa) today.
He stressed the importance of translating the party's plans into action on the ground to ensure identified supporters cast their ballots.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 for polling, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional won two. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police hunt Honda Accord driver after van driver knocked down in PJ
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Police are tracking down the driver of a black Honda Accord after a van driver was knocked down following a road dispute here yesterday.
The van driver, a local man in his 20s, suffered injuries to his elbow and knee in the incident, which was captured on video and later circulated on social media.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received a report from the van driver at 6.22pm yesterday.
He said preliminary investigations found that a disagreement had occurred between the two drivers while they were on the road.
"The van driver stopped his vehicle and asked the car driver to get out.
"However, the car driver accelerated and struck the van driver's right leg, causing him to fall onto the road and sustain injuries to his elbow and knee," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said police had also detected a video of the incident circulating on social media.
The case is being investigated under Section 334 of the Penal Code and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955.
"Police are working to locate the car driver to assist in investigations," he said.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-7966 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya and 10 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 10 states and two Federal Territories until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Baling, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Padang Terap and Sik, while in Penang, they are Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara.
In Perak, the warning covers Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Larut, Matang and Selama, and Kerian.
In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.
In Negeri Sembilan, the warning covers Seremban and Jelebu.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman (Lingga and Pantu), Betong (Kabong and Pusa), and Kuching. In Sabah, they are Kudat (Kota Marudu and Kudat), the West Coast and the Interior.
The warning was issued at 3.10pm and remains in effect until 6pm today. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan finalises Melaka seat allocation but no deal yet with other parties, says PKR sec-gen
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to reach any concrete agreement on possible political cooperation with other parties for the November 14 Melaka state election.
Datuk Fuziah Salleh, who is Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general, said, however, that seat-allocation negotiations among its three component parties — PKR, DAP and Amanah — had been finalised.
She said PH was expected to contest more than 20 state seats, with nine allocated to PKR.
“So far, there has been no concrete agreement on political cooperation with other parties. Seat allocation negotiations among PKR, DAP and Amanah have been completed,” she said.
Fuziah, who is also deputy domestic trade and cost of living minister, was speaking at a press conference after closing the Akses Peruncitan 2026 programme at a hotel here today.
She said PH chairman and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was scheduled to announce the coalition’s list of candidates in Melaka on October 24.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while PH secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two. — Bernama

Title: HRD Corp training grant applications surge after system reforms, says Ramanan
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The surge in Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications reflects the positive impact of measures taken to streamline its implementation system, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
He said the reforms have not only facilitated smoother processes but also strengthened organisational governance and transparency, although the transition required time and effort to execute properly.
“In Melaka alone, applications are nearing the 7,000 mark. This shows that more people are seizing the opportunity and demonstrates that meaningful changes are taking place.
“It is not easy to overhaul a system to make it more orderly, transparent, and aligned with good governance. It takes considerable time, and we thank the entire HRD Corp team for their dedication to carrying out these improvements,” he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp ‘Pocket Talk’ Roadshow: From Policy to the People here today.
Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Aziz.
Meanwhile, Ramanan said HRD Corp officers will monitor every training class funded through the agency’s existing levy, either on-site or virtually, to ensure courses are genuinely conducted and benefit the target groups.
“I encourage everyone to seize this opportunity, whether they are workers seeking to upskill, graduates looking for employment, or individuals wanting to build new careers,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji recalls mother borrowing RM15 for exam fees as he vows poverty will not define Sabah children
Article:
KUDAT, Oct 18 — Ensuring that poverty does not determine the fate of Sabah’s children or stand in the way of their progress has become a personal mission and commitment for Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said this resolve is rooted in his own life experiences: growing up in poverty, losing his father at a young age, working as a fisherman and a farmer and watching his mother struggle to raise him.
In an emotional account, he recalled how his mother had to borrow RM15 from relatives to pay for his Lower Certificate of Education (LCE) examination fees in 1971, as she wanted to give him a chance to break free from the cycle of poverty through education.
“Parents today face the same challenges in raising their children and providing them with an education. That is why I have firmly resolved to ensure poverty does not determine the fate of our children. Education is what can lift our children out of poverty.
“If the government has the means to remove even one obstacle from a Sabah child’s journey towards progress and success, then at the very least, we must not allow poverty to determine their fate before they even have the chance to try,” he said.
Hajiji, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, said this in his keynote address at the 2026 GRS Convention at Dewan Tun Mustapha here today.
Driven by this commitment, he said he had ensured that the state government increased the allocation for the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) to RM155 million in 2026, up from RM55 million in 2021, to fund the education of students from underprivileged backgrounds.
He said 480,000 students had so far benefitted from 14 educational assistance initiatives under the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development framework, including the BUDI cash assistance, Ihsan Computer Assistance (BAIK) and student flight ticket subsidy (SUBFLY).
Addressing the economic landscape, Hajiji stressed that the Sabah government was now ready to move into a phase of genuine development empowerment to address long-standing issues affecting the people, supported by increased state revenue that had reached RM7 billion annually.
“Efforts to address large-scale infrastructure needs are being set in motion through the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), which includes 173 Public Works Department (JKR) road network development projects and 77 projects related to water treatment plants and supply systems throughout the state,” he added.
He said the Commercial Collaboration Agreement (CCA) with Petronas in 2021 also marked a significant turning point, boosting the participation of local vendors in the oil and gas sector to 499 contracts in 2025, compared with just 133 previously.
“The state government is also committed to continuing Sabah’s pursuit of its rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) at the negotiating table with the Federal Government, guided by facts, financial data and a strong legal basis,” he said.
Hajiji said the state’s ongoing infrastructure and economic development efforts were complemented by targeted welfare initiatives, including the construction of 11,000 homes under the ‘Rumah Mesra SMJ’ initiative to assist vulnerable groups and young couples.
He added that construction would continue, with a target of building 50 ‘Rumah Mesra SMJ’ homes in each state constituency this year to ensure that the benefits of Sabah’s progress were shared by all, including rural and interior communities. — Bernama

Title: Unesco status alone won’t save silat if youth turn away, says Perak MB
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco) recognition of
silat
as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity does not guarantee its survival if younger generations increasingly distance themselves from training, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said.
He said veteran
silat
instructors and grandmasters must pass their knowledge to the next generation to keep the martial art alive and ensure it continues to be practised.
“We may have a proud
silat
heritage, but if young people turn away from the training arena, fewer will truly master and appreciate the art,” he said.
State Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah read out Saarani’s speech on his behalf at the opening of the 2026 Gema Warisan Rakan Muda X Himpunan Mahabbah Pendekar today.
Saarani said Malaysia has more than 150 identified
silat
styles, with the martial art declared a National Heritage in 2009 before gaining Unesco recognition as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019.
“Through regular training, they (youth) can develop discipline, self-confidence, mental resilience and respect for others. These qualities align with the Perak Sejahtera 2030 agenda to develop quality human capital and youth,” he said.
He also cautioned against letting differences in
silat
styles, teaching traditions, and training methods cause divisions, saying they should instead be embraced with mutual respect and a spirit of brotherhood.
“Relations between
silat
schools must continue to be nurtured to ensure the martial art remains a unifying force in society while connecting younger generations with the nation’s history and culture,” he said.
Saarani also expressed hope that the gathering will spur efforts to revive
silat
training centres, mentor young practitioners and strengthen ties between
silat
schools to preserve the martial art for future generations. — Bernama

Title: ‘We cannot sit back’: Malaysia offers aircraft to fight Indonesia forest fires despite dangerously poor visibility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysia cannot afford to stand by as raging forest fires in Indonesia send thick haze across the region, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today, as the country offered to deploy helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help contain the blazes.
But Mohamad warned that dangerously poor visibility, reportedly below 50m in affected areas, could hamper aerial firefighting operations and put pilots at risk.
“It is indeed difficult. Even the Japanese team was previously unable to do anything and has since returned to their country. But as a country affected by the situation, we cannot simply sit back and do nothing,” he said, according to
Sinar Harian
.
Speaking to reporters at the 10th National General Assembly of the National Solidarity Association (PerSoNa) in Melaka, Mohamad said the fires were burning deep in remote inland areas, making them difficult to reach by land.
Thick smoke was also preventing aircraft from operating safely.
“Aircraft cannot fly because the haze is extremely thick, with visibility of less than 50m.
“The Air Pollutant Index (API) in Kalimantan has also reached 1,000, indicating an extremely severe situation,” he said.
Mohamad stressed that the safety of pilots and other personnel must remain a priority in any proposed operation.
“We have to be careful. We cannot force pilots to fly in dangerous conditions. We will not do that,” he said.
He said discussions were under way between agencies from both countries to determine what assistance could be provided, taking into account the remote locations of the fires and the severity of the haze.
Senior officials from the Foreign Ministry, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the National Security Council (MKN) were holding talks with their Indonesian counterparts to work out the details of a possible deployment.
“Apart from offering helicopters and water-bombing aircraft capable of carrying water, they are looking at ways Malaysia can help Indonesia extinguish the forest fires that are currently raging out of control,” he said.
Mohamad said the outcome of the discussions would be presented to the Cabinet soon for approval before assistance could be extended to the Indonesian government.
The proposed assistance comes as Indonesia struggles to contain widespread forest and peatland fires that have sent thick smoke across parts of Southeast Asia.
Indonesia has agreed to accept international assistance to tackle the fires, with authorities assessing offers from neighbouring countries.
The transboundary haze has also disrupted daily life in Malaysia, with worsening air quality prompting health concerns and school closures.
In Johor, schools and educational institutions have been ordered to remain closed until October 23 as the state continues to grapple with unhealthy air quality.
The latest crisis has renewed concerns over the recurring impact of forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, which have repeatedly caused severe haze across the region.

Title: Anwar approves RM30m to resurface 600 roads in Perak, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved a special allocation of RM30 million to resurface 600 roads in residential areas across Perak, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the allocation, through the Sentuhan Kasih Istimewa YAB PMX initiative, uses the savings of the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) from recent years and is now being channelled back to improve public facilities and comfort, according to Bernama.
“In conjunction with the Perak DAP Convention, I announced on behalf of the Prime Minister a special allocation of RM30 million for road resurfacing works in residential areas across the state.
“At least 600 roads can be resurfaced through this allocation. The resurfacing works will begin next month and are expected to be fully completed before Hari Raya next year,” he said.
He said this while speaking at the 24th Perak DAP Annual Convention, officiated by DAP Secretary-General Anthony Loke here today.
The convention was attended by over 1,000 delegates.
Nga, who is also Perak DAP chairman, said the Madani Government’s commitment to safeguarding the people’s well-being is also demonstrated through various initiatives under Budget 2027 that benefit the B40 and M40 groups.
He said among these initiatives are an individual income tax exemption of RM12,000 for certain taxable incomes, as well as Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance of RM200 for 22 million recipients.
Meanwhile, Nga stressed that DAP will not compromise on issues of corruption and misappropriation despite facing various challenges.
He urged all parties to unite in rejecting corrupt practices, which he said could affect the future of the younger generation.
Nga also praised the courage of a Universiti Malaya (UM) student who voiced concerns about corruption in the country.
He, who is also a UM alumnus, said leaders must set a good example for the younger generation through their stance and actions. — Bernama

Title: Kuching, Samarahan and Serian record unhealthy API readings as haze lingers over Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 18 — Kuching, Samarahan and Serian recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm today.
According to the Natural Resource and Environment Board (NREB) website, Serian recorded the highest reading at 155, followed by Kuching 154 and Samarahan 148.
Seventeen districts recorded moderate levels. Among them, Sri Aman recorded the highest at 96, followed by Betong at 93, Lubok Antu at 90, Tebedu at 87, Lawas at 86, Lundu at 85, Kanowit at 82, Sibu at 81.
Sarikei and Samalaju and Belaga each recorded 76, while Bintulu registered 72, Mukah 71, Miri and ILP Miri 53 and Kapit 52.
Bario registered the lowest moderate reading at 51.
Meanwhile, Limbang recorded a good level of 50.
An API reading of 101 to 200 is classified as ‘Unhealthy’, 51 to 100 as ‘Moderate’ and zero to 50 as ‘Good’. — The Borneo Post

Title: E-Commerce Bill to be tabled next year to regulate online transactions, says deputy minister
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 18 — The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament at the first meeting next year to strengthen the regulation of online transactions, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh.
She said the initial draft of the Bill has been completed and is currently being refined before it is tabled.
“At present, we do not have specific legislation to regulate e-commerce. So, in most cases, we negotiate and act as intermediaries between online entrepreneurs and platform providers,” she told a press conference after closing the Retail Access Programme 2026 at a hotel here today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, said the E-Commerce Bill would be tabled at the next Parliament meeting in an effort to strengthen the accountability of online platforms and sellers.
Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme, which combines training and business matching, has helped 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to October this year.
She said the programme comprised 38 training series and 21 business matching series, involving 103 local brands and 552 stock-keeping units (SKUs).
“This programme allows entrepreneurs to present their products and understand the criteria set by supermarkets, thus identifying opportunities to enter the retail network,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Perak maintains ban on outdoor school activities despite improving API readings, says exco
Article:
