IPOH, Oct 18 — Although Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at four monitoring stations in Perak have shown a decline, outdoor school activities remain prohibited due to the current haze situation.
State Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said schools in the state were operating as usual, while teaching and learning activities must be conducted indoors.
He said the ban covers outdoor activities, such as camping and sports, while motivational programmes must also be held indoors.
“Based on the circular issued by the Ministry of Education (MOE), schools are not allowed to hold outdoor activities.
“Learning processes and other teaching activities must be carried out in classrooms only, as stipulated by the MOE,” he told reporters after representing Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad at the opening of Gema Warisan Rakan Muda X Himpunan Mahabbah Pendekar Negeri Perak 2026 here today.
Commenting on preparations for major examinations, including the KAFA Class Assessment Test (UPKK) and the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), Khairudin said any need to postpone the examinations would have to be jointly discussed by the relevant agencies.
He said the MOE, Perak State Education Department (JPN) and the relevant department responsible for overseeing the UPKK would assess the matter should the situation necessitate it.
“If there is a need to postpone these examinations, the matter may be discussed collectively by the relevant parties to ensure that their implementation does not result in students being absent.
“We can see that the API readings in Perak are improving, and we hope the UPKK, SPM and other examinations can proceed smoothly this year,” he added.
On October 15, the Perak JPN announced that all schools in the state would continue operating as usual, but parents were given the option of not sending their children to school if they had concerns about their health due to the prevailing haze.
However, parents or guardians must inform the school of their children’s absence. — Bernama

Title: Foreign minister: Nepal seeks legal amendments to expedite death certificates for 54 Malaysians
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 18 — The Nepalese government is seeking to amend the country’s laws to expedite the issuance of death certificates for 54 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following floods and landslides that hit the country in August.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Nepal’s existing laws require a waiting period of up to three years before death certificates can be issued for individuals who remain unaccounted for after a disaster.
He said Nepalese Embassy representatives informed him of the matter during a visit to his office last week.
“The Nepalese government is pursuing the legal amendments and will table them to Parliament. Failing that, it will make special arrangements to ensure death certificates can be issued without delay for the 54 Malaysians who remain unreachable,” he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the 10th National General Conference of the National Solidarity Association (PerSoNa) for the 2025 session here today.
He said the death certificates are necessary for the victims’ families to manage related affairs, including matters involving banks and insurance companies.
On Aug 26, flash floods and landslides hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the Nepal-Tibet border area after heavy rain, damaging infrastructure and communications and complicating search-and-rescue operations.
The Foreign Ministry had earlier reported that a Malaysian who could not be contacted after the disaster returned home safely on Oct 2, bringing the number of Malaysians still unaccounted for to 54.
Meanwhile, Mohamad said Malaysia is awaiting a decision by the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) and the National Security Council (MKN) on aid that can be extended to tackle forest fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, Indonesia.
He said the outcome of the discussions will be brought to the Cabinet for approval, while efforts to extinguish the fires remain challenging because they are burning in remote areas amid thick haze.
“Visibility is below 50 metres and the Air Pollutant Index in Kalimantan has reached 1,000,” he said, adding that Malaysia will assess the risks before deciding on air support and will not deploy pilots if conditions endanger their safety.
On the situation in Italy and France, Mohamad advised Malaysians travelling to the two countries to stay away from demonstrations and areas where rioters are congregating.
He said there are no travel restrictions for Italy or France at present, but Malaysians should remain cautious and comply with local authorities’ safety advice. — Bernama

Title: Tok Mat: N. Sembilan crisis won’t disrupt BN’s Melaka state election machinery
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 18 — The crisis in Negeri Sembilan is not expected to affect Barisan Nasional’s (BN) preparations for the Melaka state election next month, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said the key was to ensure that strategies drawn up by the party leadership were effectively implemented by its election machinery to secure victory, adding that good strategies not implemented will also cause plans to fail.
“We can draw up an excellent strategy that looks very good on paper, with many voters identified or categorised as BN’s fixed supporters. But if we fail to get them to turn out to vote, it means nothing.
“Their votes will not be cast,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the 10th National Conference of Persatuan Solidariti Nasional (PerSoNa).
Mohamad, who is also Foreign Minister, stressed the importance of translating the party’s plans into action on the ground to ensure that identified supporters actually cast their ballots.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 for polling, with nomination on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two. — Bernama

Title: Wisma Putra: Malaysians advised to postpone non-essential travel to France amid protests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysians have been advised to consider postponing non-essential travel to France until the situation improves amid ongoing demonstrations in major cities across the country.
In a statement issued today, the Foreign Ministry said it was closely monitoring developments, adding that currently, there have been no reports of Malaysians being involved or adversely affected by the situation.
The Embassy of Malaysia in Paris has issued an advisory urging Malaysians in France to exercise caution and remain vigilant.
“While travel to France remains unrestricted, Malaysians are advised to consider postponing non-essential travel until the situation improves,” the ministry said.
It said the embassy remained in close contact with the relevant local authorities to obtain the latest information and facilitate appropriate assistance to Malaysians should the need arise.
The ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, urged Malaysians residing in France to ensure that the embassy has their latest contact details. Malaysians who have yet to register and those planning to travel to  France were encouraged to do so through the ministry’s e-Konsular platform at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my
.
For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, Malaysians may contact the Embassy in Paris at +33145531185, its after-hours emergency helpline at +33632446571 or email:
dutyofficer@kln.gov.my
— Bernama

Title: DAP reps who fail performance targets risk losing candidacy in GE17, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — DAP representatives must meet strict key performance indicators (KPIs) or risk losing their candidacy in the next general election (GE17), party secretary-general Anthony Loke said today.
According to
Berita Harian
, Loke stressed that all DAP lawmakers must serve with integrity, discipline and commitment.
He cautioned that those who fall short of the party’s standards might be denied their candidacy letters when the next election comes around.
“If they fail to achieve the set KPIs, they will not receive the candidacy letter to contest in the upcoming election,” he said during the opening of the 24th Perak DAP Convention at the Ipoh Convention Centre.
Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming was also present at the event.
To enforce these standards, Loke explained that the party operates a rigorous monitoring system designed to keep representatives accountable and ensure they deliver for the public.
The evaluation covers a range of areas, including grassroots involvement, constituency work, community service and party activities, with a strong emphasis on a lawmaker’s physical presence in their area.
Loke noted that this monitoring framework applies continuous pressure on elected officials to live up to the mandate entrusted to them by voters.
“I believe the system we implemented is very effective,” he said, adding that Perak DAP’s representatives remain highly active on the ground.
He added that while the monitoring mechanism is applied nationwide, individual states maintain their own specific approaches.
“What I want to emphasise is that the Perak DAP monitoring system is very strict,” he said.
“I believe this approach has a positive impact when our representatives remain active on the ground. If there are any weaknesses, we will ensure improvements are made.”
Separately, when asked about how Pakatan Harapan will divide seats for the upcoming Melaka state election, Loke stated that the matter has already been settled at the state level.

Title: Authorities capture 12-foot crocodile at Teluk Nipah beach in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 18 — A 12-foot crocodile was captured at Teluk Nipah beach in Buntal here last Thursday.
The Civil Defence Force Kuching (APM Kuching), in a Facebook post, said its response team, together with personel from the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) and Nemo Hunter team, carried out the operation to capture the crocodile.
Meanwhile, in his Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the capture followed a public report from a 55-year-old man.
He expressed relief that the man who reported the discovery was unharmed.
“The successful operation highlights the importance of public cooperation in keeping our communities safe.
“Residents and visitors are reminded to stay alert near beaches, rivers and other areas where crocodiles may be present,” Siew said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Warisan leader: Tawau residents endure water disruptions of up to two weeks, urges govt to act
Article:
TAWAU, Oct 18 — Residents in several areas here have been forced to endure prolonged water supply disruptions lasting up to two weeks, prompting calls for the state government and Sabah Water Department to take immediate and comprehensive action.
Parti Warisan Tawau’s Istefan Koh said complaints had been received from residents in Bandar Sri Indah, Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai, Taman Millennium, Kongsi 10, Taman Sri Balung and other affected areas.
He said residents in Bandar Sri Indah had reportedly experienced water supply disruptions for 10 days, while those in Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai and Taman Millennium had faced disruptions lasting up to two weeks.
“The situation raises serious concerns about the management of water supply and the effectiveness of remedial measures taken by the authorities,” he said in a statement.
Istefan said prolonged disruptions had placed considerable strain on households, affecting daily activities such as cooking, bathing, washing clothes and maintaining personal hygiene.
He said the situation was particularly difficult for families with young children, senior citizens and individuals requiring special care, while small businesses dependent on a consistent water supply could also suffer operational setbacks.
“Clean water is a basic necessity, not a luxury. Residents should not have to endure days or even weeks without a reliable water supply,” he said.
Istefan urged the state government and Sabah Water Department to take concrete measures to ease the burden on affected communities, including increasing water tanker deliveries and ensuring a systematic distribution schedule, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged disruptions.
He also called on the authorities to provide transparent updates on the causes of the disruptions, ongoing recovery efforts, and the expected timeframe for the water supply to return to normal.
He said the state government should strengthen its oversight of the relevant agencies and ensure the issue was not addressed solely through temporary measures.
A comprehensive assessment of the existing infrastructure, supply capacity, distribution systems and maintenance procedures was also necessary to identify the root causes of the disruptions and prevent similar problems from recurring, he added.
Istefan said Tawau residents were not asking for more than a reliable supply of clean water to meet their daily needs.
He urged the authorities to give due attention to every complaint and ensure residents were not left waiting indefinitely without clear information on when their water supply would be restored.
“Residents need immediate action, transparent explanations and long-term solutions. The government must demonstrate its commitment through tangible action, not merely promises,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: WhatsApp scam: Miri man loses RM97,000 after fraudsters use his profile to dupe wife
Article:
MIRI, Oct 18 — A man here reported a loss of RM97,000 after fraudsters allegedly used his identity and profile picture on WhatsApp to deceive his wife into transferring funds into third-party accounts.
Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said according to a report filed yesterday, the victim’s wife received a WhatsApp message on Oct 16 from an unknown number displaying her husband’s profile.
“The wife assumed the message was sent by her husband, in which she was asked to make money payments.
“She then made two online money transfers using a company account, amounting to RM48,000 and RM49,000 respectively, into two different bank accounts,” he said in a statement.
The scam came to light after the wife inquired about the payments with her husband, who denied requesting any financial transfers.
“Subsequent checks revealed that the phone number did not belong to him and the WhatsApp chat history had completely disappeared,” said Mohd Farhan.
He said the victim promptly contacted the bank to request action on the recipient accounts before lodging a report at the Miri Central police station.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Mohd Farhan advised the public to remain vigilant against scam tactics involving impersonation through familiar profile photos.
“The public is urged to avoid making payments to third-party accounts without direct verification, and to retain transaction records,” he said.
He said suspicious phone or bank account numbers can be checked via the Check Scammers CCID portal at http://semakmule.rmp.gov.my before executing financial transactions. — The Borneo Post

Title: Budget 2027: Higher STR, SARA allocations help recipients plan spending, say beneficiaries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The RM16 billion allocation for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) financial aid under Budget 2027 has been described as a vital lifeline for recipients managing their monthly expenses.
When tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the increased allocation allows nine million STR recipients to receive SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year.
One recipient, Nor Azura Ismail, 42, said the increased allocation will ease the burden on low-income households managing family expenses, particularly the cost of essential items such as rice, cooking oil and eggs.
“This assistance helps reduce my monthly expenses significantly. Although it does not cover all my expenses, it at least eases the financial burden and helps me manage my family’s needs better.
“I hope this assistance will continue and be improved to ensure that those in need receive ongoing support in coping with the rising cost of living,” she told Bernama recently.
Nor Azura also lauded the government’s move to expand the use of SARA to purchase fresh produce and other fresh goods at 216 farmers’ markets, or tamu, operated by the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) nationwide, saying it will give recipients more shopping options.
Similarly, Muhammad Azham Zailani, 23, said the increased allocation for STR and SARA is particularly helpful for young people starting their careers who also face challenges managing their daily expenses.
Muhammad Azham, who began receiving SARA last year, said he used it to buy essential items such as rice, eggs, cooking oil, and toiletries.
“If the amount of assistance goes up, I might buy more non-perishable items, so I would not need to keep spending money on the same things,” the Menara Merdeka 118 employee said.
He said that before receiving the assistance, he had to prioritise essential purchases and delay less necessary ones to stay within his monthly budget, adding that he hoped more shops accept SARA payments to make the aid more accessible to recipients.
Civil servant Mashitah Zakiah Abdul Rahman, 30, said the SARA assistance had helped her cover daily essentials since she moved into rented accommodation away from her family.
“My budget was quite tight before I received this assistance, so I had to work out my expenses before buying necessities.
“I hope the SARA assistance will be increased from time to time to keep pace with the rising cost of living,” she said.
Eligible recipients receive STR in cash, while SARA is credited to their MyKad and can be used to buy necessities at participating shops and supermarkets. — Bernama

Title: No, QR payments are not getting a service charge from Nov 1, says Finance Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Finance Ministry today debunked a poster claiming that QR payments will start carrying a service charge from November 1.
The ministry said in a Facebook post today that the poster, which circulated under the headline “Top news today: QR to start service charge on Nov 1”, contains untrue information.
“There is no official announcement on service charges for QR as claimed in the poster,” it said.
It advised the public not to believe or share the poster.
“The public is urged to always obtain authentic information through the Finance Ministry’s official channels before sharing, to avoid the spread of fake news that could mislead society,” it said.
The ministry did not say who was behind the poster or how widely it had spread.

Title: MediAsas plan to offer financial, health safety net to Malaysia’s M40, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia’s middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges.
“Currently, a total of 340,000 private insurance policies have been surrendered by policyholders due to not being able to pay private premiums, and (more) people opt to go to government facilities; hence, the ministry comes up with this financial safety net.
“No citizen should fall into poverty just because he or she wants medical treatment; therefore, this Madani health financial protection comes forward by offering an affordable basic protection scheme,” he said in a post on the Facebook platform today.
Dzulkefly said the MediAsas Plan pilot project, held in the Klang Valley since the end of July, also allows policyholders to make flexible payments using the Employees Provident Fund Akaun Sejahtera (Akaun Dua) to ease their monthly burden.
As for vulnerable groups, he said the Tabung Bantuan Perubatan was increased by 50 per cent to RM60 million from RM40 million, specifically to cover high-priced medical devices such as bone implants and heart stents.
He said the government allocated RM80 million to the Peduli Kesihatan scheme for the B40 Group (PeKa B40) programme.
Earlier, the Ministry of Finance announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan). — Bernama

Title: Sahabat Madani Selangor to boost youth participation in community service, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Sahabat Madani Selangor initiative aims to strengthen youth participation in volunteerism and community service to support local communities.
Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the initiative was a continuation of the Sahabat Madani programme launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Penang last August.
He said the platform was intended to encourage more young people to contribute their time and energy to community-based programmes throughout Selangor.
“Activities include gotong-royong programmes organised in collaboration with local authorities, such as the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ), as well as other initiatives to assist the public.
“Sahabat Madani provides an ideal platform for young people to participate in such programmes and contribute to community development,” he told Bernama after launching the Rentap Pandan Madani 2026 Muay Thai Championship at the Muhibbah Complex here last night.
In another development, Tengku Zafrul, who is also Badminton Association of Malaysia (BAM) president, expressed hope that the national representatives who had reached the finals of the 2026 Denmark Open would emerge victorious today.
He said the progress of men’s doubles pair Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik, as well as women’s doubles pair Pearly Tan and M. Thinaah, to the finals reflected the players’ strong performances.
Earlier, Aaron and Wooi Yik became the first Malaysian pair to reach the finals after defeating South Korea’s world number one combination, Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae, 21-14, 21-18.
Pearly and Thinaah then completed Malaysia’s double qualification for the finals by overcoming China’s Bao Li Jing and Cao Zi Han 21-16, 21-14 at the SJF Bank Arena in Odense. — Bernama

Title: Civil marriage solemnisation does not usurp role of religious leaders, says JPN
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The solemnisation of civil marriages by authorised parties under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164) cannot be equated with the performance of religious rituals or regarded as taking over the role of religious leaders.
The National Registration Department (NRD) said the function was a responsibility carried out in accordance with the laws of the country.
“Every religion has its own marriage ceremonies, customs and practices, whether Buddhists, Christians, Hindus or other faiths, while the implementation of religious rituals is a matter for the followers and religious leaders concerned.
“From the perspective of national law, the marriages of non-Muslim couples governed by Act 164 must be carried out and registered in accordance with the stipulated provisions to ensure their marital status is legally recognised,” it said in a statement today.
Act 164 empowers appointed Registrars of Marriages and Assistant Registrars of Marriages to solemnise and register civil marriages.
Such marriages can be solemnised at NRD offices or places of worship and associations through authorised Assistant Registrars of Marriages, subject to the applicable legal requirements and procedures.
It said the government has always respected freedom of religion as well as the diversity of customs and cultures among Malaysians.
At the same time, compliance with civil marriage laws is important to ensure that the righrts and interests of couples, children and family institutions continue to be protected.
The NRD also reminded the public to understand the relevant facts and legal provisions before making any interpretations or disseminating information, especially on matters that touch on religious sensitivities.
“Everyone must respect the provisions of the country’s law and not make difference between civil matters and religious practices a basis for spreading inaccurate claims or misleading the public,” it added.
As such, the department reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that all civil marriage procedures continue to be carried out in an orderly and professional manner, in accordance with the law, while respecting the diversity of religions, customs and cultures in the country. — Bernama
Note: The National Registration Department is known as Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara (JPN) in Malay.

Title: Border agency praises late officer Norhazwani’s dedication, pledges family support
Article:
TUMPAT, Oct 18 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, on Thursday, was described as a hardworking and dedicated officer.
AKPS Deputy Director-General (Operations) SAC Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M. Nasir said Norhazwani, who joined the agency on July 1 after transferring from the Customs Department, had performed well and was committed to her duties.
“From the work perspective, she had no problems. She was a very good officer, hardworking and committed to her duties,” he told reporters at Norhazwani’s family residence in Kampung Banjir, Telaga Lanas, Pengkalan Kubor, here last night.
He said Norhazwani frequently worked overtime and had two children who still required attention and family support.
Mohd Nasaruddin said AKPS had received no information about any problems Norhazwani might have been facing before the incident.
He said AKPS Kelantan personnel, including those stationed in Rantau Panjang and Pengkalan Kubor, had contributed financial assistance to the family, while the agency would consider further welfare support, including death benefits and counselling.
On Thursday, Norhazwani Ibrahim was found dead at the KLIA quarters, and a suspect surrendered to the police later that night. — Bernama

Title: Anwar congratulates Low Zi Yu-Genevie Lim on ending Malaysia’s 34-year wait for badminton World Junior title
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national women’s junior doubles pair Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on their outstanding achievement in winning the title at the 2026 World Junior Badminton Championships in Cairo, Egypt.
He described their success in ending Malaysia’s 34-year wait for the title as a tremendous source of pride and a historic milestone for the sport in the country.
“An achiecement to be proud of! Congratulations to Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on winning the girls’ doubles title at the World Junior Badminton Championships. A new chapter in the history of Malaysian badminton!” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also urged both shuttlers to maintain their excellent form and further enhance the country’s standing on the international stage.
“Syabas (well done), keep up the momentum and continue to make Malaysia proud!” he said.
In yesterday’s final at the Cairo International Stadium, the second-seeded Malaysians defeated Japan’s Nijika Kamata-Shizuku Kashio 15-7, 9-15, 15-12.
The historic win ended Malaysia’s 34-year wait for its maiden girls’ doubles title since the world junior meet was first held in 1992. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails Siti Nurhaliza’s soulful Gema Bumantara concert as 63,000 braved rain to attend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin on her exceptional and soulful performance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara show last night.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar also congratulated the entire production team on the success of the concert.
“It was a pleasure to enjoy Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza’s performance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara last night, which beautifully celebrated the rich artistic heritage of the Nusantara.
“Despite the rain, everyone in attendance stayed until the end of the performance. Bravo, Datuk Seri Siti, and bravo to her dedicated fans. Congratulations to Datuk Seri Siti and the entire production team for delivering such an exceptional and soulful performance,” he said.
Anwar said he believed that arts and culture held a special place in the hearts of the people and wanted the nation’s heritage to continue to be preserved and cherished by younger generations.
“We will continue to drive the nation’s progress while safeguarding our cultural roots and national identity,” he said.
Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara, organised by SN Legacy, drew 63,000 concertgoers to the TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil last night despite the rain. — Bernama

Title: Sister bars in-laws from attending funeral of border agency officer allegedly killed by husband, says they didn’t ask about children
Article:
TUMPAT, Oct 18 — The family of Norhazwani Ibrahim, a 35-year-old border agency officer allegedly murdered by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, has refused to allow his parents and relatives to attend her funeral here, saying they cannot accept what he is accused of doing.
The victim’s elder sister, Marlina, 46, told
Utusan Malaysia
that the family had also barred the husband’s relatives from visiting the deceased before her burial.
“We really cannot accept it if her in-laws or the husband’s family come.
“I personally would not allow them to attend the funeral or the burial,” she was quoted as saying.
Marlina said the family was particularly hurt that none of the husband’s relatives had contacted them last night to ask about the welfare of the couple’s two young daughters, aged six and five, following their mother’s death.
Marlina said she was still struggling to come to terms with the death of her youngest sister, Norhazwani, who was the youngest of nine siblings.
She recalled speaking to Norhazwani over the phone last Tuesday, just two days before she was allegedly killed.
“How could he bring himself to kill his own wife?” Marlina asked, expressing regret that she had not managed to see her sister during her last visit to their Kelantan hometown on October 5.
Marlina said she had contacted Norhazwani a few days later to invite her for a meal, but her sister told her she had already returned to Nilai.
Norhazwani had planned to visit the family again in December, Marlina said.
The officer, who worked for the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency, was buried at Tanjong Cemetery in Pengkalan Kubor at about 2am today.

Title: Khaled Nordin begins four-day working visit to Japan to strengthen defence ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin’s official working visit to Japan, which begins today, is expected to bring tangible benefits to the country’s defence while enhancing mutual understanding in addressing regional security challenges.
He said the four-day visit, anchored by the Malaysia-Japan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, aims to strengthen defence ties and expand the scope of cooperation between the two nations.
Mohamed Khaled, who safely arrived at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, said key engagements during the visit include bilateral meetings with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi.
“I am also scheduled to attend a ceremony for the signing of grant assistance documents under the Japanese government’s Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme,” he said in a post on his official Facebook page.
He said the visit woud also include a meeting with Japan’s Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA), as well as a visit to Japanese defence company, Toshiba.
Earlier, Mohamed Khaled was received upon his arrival in Tokyo by Malaysia’s Ambassador to Japan Datuk Ahmad Rozian Abd Ghani and Malaysia’s Defence Attaché in Tokyo, Capt Mohamad Fazri Ibrahim.
Also part of the delegation are the Defence Ministry’s deputy secretary-general (Policy) Datuk Mohd Yani Daud and Malaysian Armed Forces Headquarters Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Datuk Seri Muhammad Huzaimi Sabri. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: BN to unveil candidate list on Oct 28, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 18 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will announce the list of candidates who will contest in the Melaka State Election (PRN) on October 28, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Ab Rauf, who is also the Melaka BN Chairman, said the line-up of candidates put forward will shoulder a heavy responsibility to continue the mandate’s continuity and ensure the party’s victory in the election.
“So, Insya-Allah, I will make the candidate announcement on October 28. Whoever the candidate may be, that is the candidate who will carry the waves of Umno and BN’s struggle,” he said in his speech at the launch of the Tangga Batu Parliamentary Election Machinery in Sungai Udang here last night.
Also present were Kedah Umno Liaison Body Chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid, Melaka MCA Chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong, and Tangga Batu Umno Division Chief Datuk Rais Yasin.
The Election Commission (EC) has set polling day for the Melaka state election on November 14, while nomination day is set for October 31 and early voting on November 10.
The previous Melaka state election held in 2021 saw BN winning 21 out of 28 seats, thereby forming the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional won two seats. — Bernama

Title: Wrong Nani, wrong story: Presenter Nani Roc tells online sleuths she’s not in the khalwat story
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Presenter and influencer Nani Roslan has denied being the woman detained alongside former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad in a Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) raid last Thursday for alleged
khalwat —
a Syariah offence involving an unmarried Muslim man and woman found alone together in a secluded place or in close proximity.
She posted a denial in an Instagram Story last night after her name, photos and videos were pulled into online speculation about the case.
“I am not that woman. I never expected to have to come forward to explain this,” she said.
Nani, whose full name is Nur Syazwani Roslan and who is better known as Nani Roc, is a freelance emcee and voice-over artiste who started out as a broadcast journalist and news reader in 2010.
Born in Johor and raised in Shah Alam, she runs her own talent company, NaniRoc Talents Enterprise, and co-hosts the
Kata Kita
podcast with actress Diana Danielle.
She also co-hosted the
Lebih Masa
podcast with Nik Nazmi, an arrangement she said ended on September 30.
Nani said she spoke up only because the speculation had escalated into lewd and degrading remarks about her as a woman.
She also rejected claims that she was involved in any plan linked to the incident, calling them completely untrue.
She said her work as a professional presenter had put her in front of people from all backgrounds, and that some parties had blocked her or dropped her at the last minute, even before this controversy, because they associated her jobs with certain political parties.
“Doing my job does not mean I am promoting any particular party’s political views,” she said.
She added that social media users are free to be curious, but they must stay respectful.
“Freedom of speech is not a licence to defame others, which can have legal consequences,” she said.
Nik Nazmi, a co-founder of Bersama, confirmed yesterday that he was one of two people detained by Jais in Petaling Jaya on October 15, saying he was with a woman who is not his
muhrim
(a close relative he is forbidden to marry under Islamic law), during the raid.
He apologised to his wife, family and party members.
Bersama has since suspended him from all official party activities for three months, from October 20 to January 19, 2027.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who is also Selangor menteri besar, has denied claims that PKR plotted a
khalwat t
rap against Nik Nazmi, a party member for almost 21 years until he left in May.
The Selangor Islamic Religious Council has likewise rejected suggestions that the detention was a Jais “frame-up”, saying no one is above the law.

Title: Selangor studying retention ponds, drainage upgrades for Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang, says exco
Article:
KLANG, Oct 18 — The Selangor state government is conducting a detailed study to identify critical locations for new retention ponds and drainage upgrades to address flash floods, particularly in urban areas.
State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said the study would focus on areas requiring urgent solutions, including Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang.
“Selangor is currently receiving various flood mitigation projects from the federal government worth more than RM4 billion, some of which are being implemented or nearing completion, while others are still in the planning stages.
“We acknowledge that flash flood issues still need to be addressed, particularly in urban areas such as Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang. We will therefore study and identify the critical locations for the construction of retention ponds or the widening of drainage systems,” he told reporters after officiating the Selangor State Budget Town Hall Programme: Kita Anak Muda 2026 here today.
When tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an allocation of RM100 million for the development of retention ponds and river maintenance to reduce flash flood risks in the Klang Valley.
The federal and Selangor state governments also agreed on five key measures to address flooding, including assessing the capacity of the Batu Dam and Klang Gates Dam to meet water requirements over the next 30 years.
Izham said that besides constructing retention ponds and upgrading drainage systems, he had also proposed alternative flood mitigation measures, including a ‘water highway’ in the Klang Valley.
He said the proposal had previously been presented to the Prime Minister, who requested that it be studied thoroughly before being included in Water Master Plan 2.
Meanwhile, Izham said the federal government had approved RM40 million to address flash floods around Bukit Raja, including i-City. However, the upgrading project was still at the design stage and would require more time before implementation.
He said his portfolio was also expected to receive additional allocations under the Selangor Budget 2027, to be tabled next month, for road and flood management projects under the Public Works Department (JKR) and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS).
“We do indeed have high-value projects. The matter will be announced by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari later,” he said.
On frequent accidents along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Izham said a proposal to upgrade the route was being finalised.
He said the proposals included increasing the number of lanes from two to three, including at intersections, although implementation would involve relatively high costs. — Bernama
